description: The de-risking spike: build and execute OUR OWN ggml compute graph for the tiny MoE forward pass (NOT llama_decode) and compare against libllama as oracle on the SAME gguf and prompt. This proves the single riskiest unknown - that we can reproduce llama's math through a ggml graph we construct ourselves. Throwaway code under spike/engine_core/ (binary gitignored, source kept, like the existing spike/ dirs). Depends on FEAT-001.
steps: Create spike/engine_core/ . Add the Coaade SPDX header and a 'SPIKE -- do not ship' banner to every source file, mirroring spike/stream_decode/spike_stream.cpp.

Add a gitignore entry for the new spike binary: append a line '/spike/**/spike_engine' to the existing 'Throwaway spike binaries' block in /projects/sandbox/strataflow/.gitignore (next to spike_touch/spike_stream/spike_baseline).

Write spike/engine_core/spike_oracle.cpp: load /projects/sandbox/moe.gguf via llama_model_load_from_file + llama_init_from_model (CPU), tokenize a fixed prompt (e.g. the model's BOS plus a short fixed id sequence; reuse the tokenize approach in src/model/ggml_model.cpp), run ONE llama_decode for the first token, capture the full logits vector via llama_get_logits_ith(ctx,-1) and the greedy argmax token id. This is the ORACLE. Write the logits to a side file (e.g. /projects/sandbox/oracle_logits.bin) and print the argmax id and top-5 (id,logit).

Pull the weights the engine graph needs out of the loaded model via ggml. Use the model's tensors directly: llama exposes them through the loaded ggml context / tensors by name. Investigate how to retrieve a weight tensor by name from the loaded llama_model (e.g. walk the model's ggml buffers, or load tensor data independently via gguf_init_from_file with no_alloc=false and ggml_get_tensor by name - the simplest reliable path for a spike is to open the gguf a second time with no_alloc=false so ggml allocates and fills all tensors, then fetch each by its GGUF name: token_embd.weight, output_norm.weight, output.weight, and per layer blk.N.{attn_norm,attn_q,attn_k,attn_v,attn_output,ffn_norm,ffn_gate_inp,ffn_gate_exps,ffn_down_exps,ffn_up_exps}.weight). Confirm shapes against make_tiny_moe_gguf.py (n_embd=32, n_head=4, n_ff=64, 8 experts top-2, head_dim=8).

Write spike/engine_core/spike_engine.cpp (OUR graph): ggml_init a context (no_alloc=true for the graph build context), build a ggml_cgraph that reproduces the llama-arch forward for the SAME single token at position 0, following third_party/llama.cpp/src/models/llama.cpp and build_moe_ffn in src/llama-graph.cpp. Required ops per the reference: build the input embedding (ggml_get_rows of token_embd by the token id); per layer il in 0..1: RMSNorm (ggml_rms_norm eps=1e-5 then ggml_mul attn_norm), Q=mul_mat(wq,cur) K=mul_mat(wk,cur) V=mul_mat(wv,cur) reshaped to heads, ggml_rope_ext on Q and K (NEOX/NORM type per the gguf rope settings; n_rot=head_dim=8, freq_base/scale from defaults 10000/1), attention: scores=mul_mat(K,Q) scaled by 1/sqrt(head_dim), causal mask for a single position (trivial - 1 position), ggml_soft_max_ext, context=mul_mat(V,probs), reshape, output proj mul_mat(wo), residual add; RMSNorm ffn_norm; MoE: logits=mul_mat(ffn_gate_inp,cur) [n_expert,1], ggml_soft_max, ggml_argsort_top_k(2) -> selected_experts [2,1], weights via ggml_get_rows on reshaped probs then normalize by sum (ggml_sum_rows, clamp 6.103515625e-5, ggml_div), up=ggml_mul_mat_id(ffn_up_exps,cur,ids) gate=ggml_mul_mat_id(ffn_gate_exps,cur,ids) ggml_swiglu_split(gate,up) experts=ggml_mul_mat_id(ffn_down_exps,...), weight each expert by weights and sum over the n_expert_used dim; residual add; final output_norm RMSNorm; logits=mul_mat(output,cur). Mark the final logits ggml_set_output.

Allocate the graph with ggml_gallocr (ggml_gallocr_new(ggml_backend_cpu_buffer_type()); ggml_gallocr_alloc_graph), set the position / input tensors, and execute on the CPU backend: ggml_backend_cpu_init, ggml_backend_cpu_set_n_threads(1) for determinism, ggml_backend_graph_compute(backend, gf). Read our logits tensor back.

Compare OUR logits against the oracle logits on the same model+prompt+position: compute max absolute difference and mean absolute difference across the vocab, and compare the greedy argmax token id. Print: engine argmax, oracle argmax, match (yes/no), max|delta|, mean|delta|, and the top-5 of each. Treat tight tolerance (max abs diff < ~1e-3 on this F32 tiny model) and identical argmax as PASS.

Make the comparison the spike's exit status: return 0 and print 'SPIKE PASS' only when the argmax ids match; otherwise print 'SPIKE FAIL' with the first divergence point and return non-zero. If logits diverge, instrument intermediate tensors (dump cur after each layer / after attention vs after MoE) to pinpoint WHERE the math first diverges - that localization is a required output, not optional.

Build the spike standalone (NOT via CMake) with the verified pattern, compiling both TUs into one binary (or two binaries sharing a header): g++ -std=c++17 -fopenmp -I third_party/llama.cpp/include -I third_party/llama.cpp/ggml/include -I third_party/llama.cpp/ggml/src spike/engine_core/*.cpp -o spike/engine_core/spike_engine -L build/debug/lib -lllama -lggml -lggml-cpu -lggml-base -lpthread -lm . Run: ./spike/engine_core/spike_engine /projects/sandbox/moe.gguf .

If a FULL forward proves too large for one spike, FALL BACK to the critical sub-part per the user instruction: build+execute OUR ggml graph for ONE transformer block (attention + MoE FFN with ggml_mul_mat_id over the stacked expert tensors) using weights pulled from the loaded model, and compare that block's output tensor against the same block computed via libllama (e.g. by reading llama's named intermediate via its callback / or a hand reference). Still report measured agreement and the divergence point. Document clearly in findings which scope was achieved (full forward vs single block).

Write spike/engine_core/README.md recording: exact build command, run command, what was proven, the measured max|delta| / mean|delta| / argmax agreement vs the oracle, and - if divergence was found - exactly where. Record the same summary in this feature's findings field.
acceptance_criteria: spike/engine_core/spike_engine compiles with the documented standalone g++ command and runs against /projects/sandbox/moe.gguf.

The spike constructs and executes a ggml_cgraph built BY THE SPIKE (ggml_mul_mat/ggml_mul_mat_id/ggml_rms_norm/ggml_rope_ext/ggml_soft_max_ext etc.) and runs it on the ggml CPU backend via ggml_backend_graph_compute - it does NOT call llama_decode to produce the engine result.

The spike loads the oracle result from llama_decode on the SAME gguf and prompt and prints a quantitative comparison: engine vs oracle greedy argmax token id, max absolute logit difference, and mean absolute logit difference (or, in single-block fallback mode, the block output tensor agreement).

The spike prints 'SPIKE PASS' with exit 0 when the engine and oracle greedy argmax ids match within tolerance; on mismatch it prints 'SPIKE FAIL' and localizes the first divergent intermediate tensor.
spike/engine_core/README.md and the findings field record the measured agreement numbers and the achieved scope (full forward or single-block fallback).
The spike binary is gitignored (/spike/**/spike_engine) and only source + README are left tracked.
verification: g++ -std=c++17 -fopenmp -I third_party/llama.cpp/include -I third_party/llama.cpp/ggml/include -I third_party/llama.cpp/ggml/src spike/engine_core/*.cpp -o spike/engine_core/spike_engine -L build/debug/lib -lllama -lggml -lggml-cpu -lggml-base -lpthread -lm
git status --porcelain (confirm spike/engine_core/spike_engine is NOT listed as untracked - it is gitignored)
findings: PASS. Scope achieved: FULL forward (both transformer blocks: attn + MoE FFN + final norm + lm_head), NOT the single-block fallback. The spike (spike/engine_core/spike_engine.cpp) builds and executes OUR OWN ggml_cgraph (ggml_get_rows embd; per layer ggml_rms_norm+ggml_mul, ggml_mul_mat Q/K/V, ggml_rope_ext NORM mode 0 n_dims=head_dim=8 freq_base=10000 freq_scale=1, permute + ggml_mul_mat(k,q) + ggml_soft_max_ext(scale=1/sqrt(8)) + ggml_mul_mat(v,kq) attention, output proj + residual; ggml_rms_norm ffn_norm; MoE: ggml_mul_mat gate_inp -> ggml_soft_max -> ggml_argsort_top_k(2) -> ggml_get_rows weights normalized by clamped(6.103515625e-5) ggml_sum_rows via ggml_div; ggml_mul_mat_id up/gate exps, ggml_swiglu_split, ggml_mul_mat_id down exps, per-expert weight + sum over n_expert_used; residual; final ggml_rms_norm output_norm; ggml_mul_mat lm_head) and runs it on the ggml CPU backend via ggml_backend_graph_compute (ggml_backend_cpu_set_n_threads=1). It does NOT call llama_decode for the engine result. Weights pulled via a second gguf_init_from_file(no_alloc=false) + ggml_get_tensor by GGUF name; shapes verified at runtime (token_embd ne=[32,264], output ne=[32,264], blk.0.ffn_gate_exps ne=[32,64,8] matching n_embd=32,n_ff=64,n_expert=8). Measured engine-vs-oracle on moe.gguf, single BOS token at position 0: greedy argmax MATCH (both token id 71); max absolute logit delta = 5.3167e-5; mean absolute logit delta = 1.2078e-5 across the 264-wide vocab; deterministic (identical across runs). PASS = identical argmax AND max|delta| 5.3e-5 < 1e-3 tol. No divergence found. The ~5e-5 (not bit-exact) residual is expected and benign: the oracle llama_decode path uses fused flash attention (ggml_flash_attn_ext, F16 intermediates) while the engine graph uses explicit F32 mul_mat+soft_max_ext attention; agreement to 5e-5 confirms the math (including MoE top-2 routing via ggml_mul_mat_id over stacked expert tensors, the riskiest part) is equivalent. Spike reads back per-layer intermediates (after attn+residual and after MoE+residual, both layers) for divergence localization; all finite and in range. Build: g++ -std=c++17 -fopenmp -I third_party/llama.cpp/include -I third_party/llama.cpp/ggml/include -I third_party/llama.cpp/ggml/src spike/engine_core/*.cpp -o spike/engine_core/spike_engine -L build/debug/lib -lllama -lggml -lggml-cpu -lggml-base -lpthread -lm; compiled clean, exit 0, prints SPIKE PASS. Binary gitignored via /spike/**/spike_engine; only source + README tracked. The 11-suite ctest and cmake build remain green (no src/ changes). README at spike/engine_core/README.md records the same.
